title: Simultaneous Learning and Optimization via Misspecified Saddle Point Problems
abstract: arXiv:2510.05241v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study a class of misspecified saddle point (SP) problems, where the optimization objective depends on an unknown parameter that must be learned concurrently from data. Unlike existing studies that assume parameters are fully known or pre-estimated, our framework integrates optimization and learning into a unified formulation, enabling a more flexible problem class. To address this setting, we propose two algorithms based on the accelerated primal-dual (APD) by Hamedani & Aybat 2021. In particular, we first analyze the naive extension of the APD method by directly substituting the evolving parameter estimates into the primal-dual updates; then, we design a new learning-aware variant of the APD method that explicitly accounts for parameter dynamics by adjusting the momentum updates. Both methods achieve a provable convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(\log K / K)$, while the learning-aware approach attains a tighter $\mathcal{O}(1)$ cons

translated_title: 基于误设定鞍点问题的学习与优化同步进行
translated_abstract: 我们研究一类误设定的鞍点（SP）问题，其中优化目标依赖于一个必须从数据中同步学习的未知参数。与现有研究中假设参数完全已知或预先估计的做法不同，我们的框架将优化与学习整合到一个统一的公式化中，从而实现了一个更灵活的问题类别。为解决这一设定，我们基于Hamedani与Aybat（2021）的加速原始-对偶（APD）方法提出了两种算法。具体而言，我们首先通过将不断演化的参数估计直接代入原始-对偶更新，分析了APD方法的朴素扩展；随后，我们设计了一种新的“学习感知”APD变体，通过调整动量更新来显式考虑参数动态。两种方法均实现了可证明的 $\mathcal{O}(\log K / K)$ 收敛率，而学习感知方法则获得了更优的 $\mathcal{O}(1)$ 约束（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个将优化与参数学习统一处理的误设定鞍点问题框架，并设计了两种基于加速原始-对偶（APD）方法的算法，均达到 $\mathcal{O}(\log K/K)$ 收敛率，其中学习感知变体通过调整动量更新显式建模参数动态，并获得更优的 $\mathcal{O}(1)$ 约束保证。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unified framework for misspecified saddle point problems that integrates optimization with concurrent parameter learning, and develops two algorithms based on the accelerated primal-dual (APD) method—both achieving $\mathcal{O}(\log K/K)$ convergence, with a learning-aware variant that explicitly accounts for parameter dynamics through adjusted momentum updates and attains a tighter $\mathcal{O}(1)$ constraint guarantee.
